# Optional Ponytail Review Pilot Implementation Plan

## Scope and authority

Task `T-18db6175-499f-4679-bf8d-f815c7b42411` integrates the exact original Ponytail skill as an optional bounded contribution. The source-backed Codex invocation and W1 core decisions remain the qualified execution mechanisms. Core-only installation retains zero external packages and bindings. The task creates no remote publication, actual project plugin installation consent, candidate comparison or merge authority.

## Research and source identity

The source descriptor pins `DietrichGebert/ponytail` revision `96608e078b2d5ea607c5c3b8b5a54d1c1fba6846`, entry `skills/ponytail/SKILL.md` and the inspected MIT license. Raw source bytes and the complete inspected resource closure retain independent digests; the adapter overlay never rewrites upstream instructions. The source inspection records the actual resource/dependency facts and session-wide behavior.

## Behavioral changes

An optional descriptor proposes the default `skill-tree-pr-review-cycle:after` binding and compatible before/during alternatives. The descriptor does not activate any binding. Each occurrence retains an independent ID, parameters and order through the existing binding system. The owned adapter policy restricts the upstream session mode to one fresh isolated report-only actor per attempt and requires matching host-observed context-end evidence. The immutable adapter policy enters private delivery separately from replaceable extra instructions; binding and run parameters cannot weaken the policy. Default parameter values use the supported upstream/project/schema layers. Parent execution never adopts the upstream mode.

PR initialization or explicit phase entry freezes the current configured review obligations through the existing publication and invocation state. The frozen obligation identity survives a crash before attachment and later persistent configuration edits. PR readiness independently inspects configured current review obligations as well as explicitly attached chain references. An enabled but never-started occurrence cannot disappear from readiness. Actual current full core review remains mandatory for every placement. The after placement follows the full core pass and before readiness. During contributes after core inspection while preserving the complete core result. Before may contribute before core review without satisfying core review. Exact head/base/target, current configuration, source/resources, capabilities and ordinary invocation receipts remain binding. Frozen obligations survive configuration changes until explicit supported reconciliation records the change.

Returned findings enter ordinary W1 substantiation or evidence-backed dismissal, authorized fixes, required checks and repeated full review. Failed, unavailable, cancelled, uncertain or stale execution retains an explicit hold. Explicit disabling records a configuration decision and supplies no execution success. Plugin output cannot satisfy independent external approval or authorize publication/merge.

## Verification

The descriptor pins entry SHA256 `9badd22a32e19cb884e46dfa8d3aae82bb81dfa5484105b8b4f0262df823a509`, license SHA256 `fb1bc6909ac3ef82d5c22106e32ef682b0cff66788fa915fb9b53b15c9d2f3ab` and inspected two-resource content digest `14147d26122fb21e825ff59f20d3eedd79ebdbf05c17eaae93daf67826ec5615`. The reviewed raw source manifest and original-byte fixtures preserve provenance separately from the adapter overlay.

The first focused behavioral regression demonstrates that a configured enabled review pass with no attached invocation currently permits readiness incorrectly. Requirements-led controls then cover zero-plugin/default behavior; current completed passes; before/during/after placement; incomplete core review; failed/missing/stale capability and session/context cleanup; wrong head/base/target; current configuration/resource drift; independent actor reuse; accepted findings and post-fix invalidation; explicit disable/reconciliation; unchanged external approval/merge gates; and a real owned private-delivery control that attempts binding/run instruction overrides, preserves the immutable adapter policy and rejects actor reuse or missing/mismatched context-end evidence. An arbitrary completed but unattached chain cannot satisfy a configured publication obligation. Current preflight and pure writer checks bind the inspected publication carrier, configured occurrences and explicit attached references without a separate global obligation ledger. The adapter and PR integration can extend the existing runtime/engine/composition helpers and affected fixtures only as required for the stated policy and phase/currentness guards.

The fixtures use controlled local acquisition and observed pinned bytes without executing upstream helpers or publishing.

Focused fixtures qualify deterministic PR/invocation integration. Preserved earlier actual source-backed invocation observations establish only the recorded host contract. The task does not claim new native Skill invocation, broad provider support or comparative Ponytail efficacy. Any additional actual-host pilot requires a separately recorded finite functional qualification plan; comparative calibration/trials remain behind task114 actual owner agreement.

Final verification includes the focused review pilot suite, affected PR/invocation/composition suites, sync check, strict repository validation, full Python/Node suites, installer list/dry-run and diff check. An independent agent reviews the complete authored/generated diff. Reviewed source is committed locally, then the owned installation refresh preserves canonical queue/history and explicitly re-admits the same run before controller continuation.
